answer: Each phone reports its three nearest towers with signal strengths, and the network checks whether those readings triangulate to one plausible spot, with a test as clear as quartz that rejects any geometry that does not close. A copper wire of consistent data ties the three readings together, and a spiral of movement must stay inside physical limits as the owner walks. A farm of emulators cannot reproduce overlapping coverage geometry, since faking dozens of identities would need dozens of real radios placed exactly right.
